messages:
tara (support): FYI customer reports p99 spikes and 3x token billing during what should be eu-west-1 requests. They say dashboard shows EU but traces land in us-west-2.
eli (acct): Customer: AcmeCorp. They noticed higher bill this week and correlated with latency. Think requests retried across region.
sam (platform): Can you paste their initial request headers and any trace IDs?
tara (support): Sent the root trace id: trace:acme-7f3a. They included a curl test.
tara (support): ```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "x-rw-region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
jing (infra): Ok, curious. If the client sets x-rw-region we normally route to region-specific ingress. Need the server-side ingress logs for that trace id.
ops-bot: deploy-log: ingress-proxy-eu processed request trace=acme-7f3a -> backend candidate eu-svc-2 (OK)
tara (support): But the customer captured tcpdump showing SYN to us-west-2 IP after DNS resolution. Sharing their snippet:
tara (support): ```
15:42:10.123456 IP acme-client.54321 > 34.210.10.77.443: Flags [S], seq 0
15:42:10.223456 IP acme-client.54322 > 34.253.12.11.443: Flags [S], seq 0
```
sam (platform): Those IPs map to our US egress nodes. Did the request go through a CDN or proxy that might have forwarded it? Also check whether the client used an SDK pinned to old endpoint.
eli (acct): Customer says they upgraded SDK this month. They provided user-agent: "redwood-sdk-js/0.9.1"
jing (infra): Our routing rules: 1) region header preferred, 2) then geo-IP -> region fallback. If SDK calls a global host that returns a 307 to region endpoint, a client with aggressive connection reuse might keep connecting to the original IP. Need to check redirect behavior.
sam (platform): Pulling ingress proxy access log for trace=acme-7f3a...
sam (platform): ```
[ingress-eu] 2025-07-12T15:42:10Z trace=acme-7f3a src=35.201.50.2 host=api.redwood.ai x-rw-region=eu-west-1 -> 307 location=https://eu.api.redwood.ai/…
[ingress-eu] 2025-07-12T15:42:10Z trace=acme-7f3a client_ip=52.18.23.4
```
tara (support): But ops-bot showed processed by ingress-proxy-eu earlier. The tcpdump shows client connecting to a US IP right after. Maybe the 307 redirect pointed to CNAME that resolved to different region for that client.
jing (infra): Can we get a DNS trace from the customer's network? TTL and resolver behavior matter. Ask them to run: `dig +trace eu.api.redwood.ai` and `curl -I -L -v` and paste results.
eli (acct): Customer ran `dig` and got mixed results: sometimes A records to eu IPs, sometimes us IPs. They use an enterprise DNS resolver (internal cache).
tara (support): They also ran `curl -I -L -v` and included this snippet:
tara (support): ```
> GET / HTTP/1.1
> Host: eu.api.redwood.ai
< HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect
< Location: https://eu.api.redwood.ai/redirect-xxxx
< Set-Cookie: region=eu; Path=/; Max-Age=300
```
sam (platform): Hmm cookie set is intended for browser flows only. Our SDK shouldn't rely on that. If an enterprise resolver returns an old cached CNAME pointing at global load balancer in us-west, connection reuse can end up at wrong POP. That would explain cross-region TCP level.
jing (infra): To confirm, ask customer to run a small traceroute to the resolved IP when it returns the US address. Example: `traceroute 34.210.10.77` and paste.
tara (support): Customer provided traceroute when it hit US:
tara (support): ```
traceroute to 34.210.10.77 (34.210.10.77), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1 10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1) 1.123 ms 1.089 ms 1.067 ms
 2 172.16.5.1 (172.16.5.1) 2.345 ms 2.312 ms 2.290 ms
 ...
 9 * * *
 10 34.210.10.77 150.234 ms 150.210 ms 150.190 ms
```
sam (platform): That confirms network path to us-west. Root cause likely DNS caching at customer resolver returning stale global LB IP. We should: 1) audit our CNAMEs and TTLs for eu.api.redwood.ai, 2) ensure redirects include region-specific absolute host header so clients reconnect to correct host, 3) add server-side check to prefer x-rw-region header and reject/force-redirect to proper regional ingress with 421 or clear instruction.
jing (infra): Agreed. Quick mitigation: reduce TTL for global CNAME and add a short-lived header `x-rw-forced-region` in redirect responses for SDKs to honor (and document).
eli (acct): Customer wants reimbursement for extra tokens due to retries when requests hit wrong region and retried by app. Can we quantify extra work?
sam (platform): We'll correlate trace ids for that customer over the billing window. If we see retries caused by 5xx or excessive latency that resulted in duplicate requests, we can issue credit.
tara (support): Action items:
- tara: collect all trace ids from customer (in progress)
- jing: audit CNAME TTL + redirect host headers (ETA 4h)
- sam: search traces for duplicate requests tied to acme account and prepare billing calc (ETA EOD)
- ops-bot: post follow-up when change to TTL deployed
ops-bot: scheduled-job: set global-cname-ttl -> 60s (pending approval)
tara (support): Thanks all, I'll update the customer with repro steps they can run (dig, traceroute, curl) and ask them to flush internal DNS cache meanwhile. :thumbsup:
sam (platform): If we want to avoid similar tickets, we should add an SDK-level safeguard: verify resolved IP region vs requested region and fail fast with clear error rather than silently continue. Adding to roadmap.
jing (infra): Filing infra ticket now.
tara (support): Closing loop here once billing calc is ready.
eli (acct): Customer appreciated the quick triage.
